backups.destination: BACKUP_DIR, else STORAGE_PATH/backups — the same disk as the database, so this protects against logical loss, not disk loss (see spof)
backups.postgres: pg_dump when DATABASE_URL is set. The image does not ship pg_dump; scripts/backup.sh names that and exits 2 rather than writing a file that is not a dump.
backups.restore_drill: tests/test_backup_restore.py restores what scripts/backup.sh produces (dump, wipe, restore, planted row readable)
backups.sqlite: SQLite online backup of STORAGE_PATH/platform.db: the sqlite3 CLI when installed, else the Python stdlib backup() API on the same file — the image ships python, not the CLI, so both legs work in the deployed container

jobs: test: python -m pytest tests, plus an import of app.main with an empty environment
bench: scripts/bench.py, p95 under the 500ms budget
image: docker build, then boot the built container on a self-chosen PORT (8931), probe /health, /metrics, / and /console/, and wait for the image's own HEALTHCHECK to report healthy

health.probe: HEALTHCHECK CMD python3 -c urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:'+os.environ.get('PORT','8000')+'/health') — interval 10s, timeout 3s, start-period 40s, retries 3
health.render: healthCheckPath: /health (same probe; 503 takes the instance out)
health.start_period_reason: the entrypoint applies migrations before uvicorn binds, so the first probe must tolerate that window
health.where_it_answers_before_traffic: the HEALTHCHECK follows $PORT, the port the entrypoint binds (docker run -e PORT=8931 in CI proves it); /health answers 503 until STORAGE_PATH is writable, platform.db opens and alembic is at head

logging.f13: structured request lines are ASCII JSON; emoji stripped

assets./: app/static/index.html — the dependency-free console, copied from the tree

packaging.console_stage: node:18-slim: npm ci against the committed frontend/package-lock.json, npx tsc --noEmit, npx vite build --outDir dist --emptyOutDir. A lockfile out of step with package.json fails the build. vite's base is /console/ (frontend/vite.config.ts), so the emitted index.html asks for /console/assets/*, which is where app/main.py mounts the bundle; with vite's default base it asked the root for /assets/* and the page 404ed its own JavaScript.
packaging.entrypoint: scripts/entrypoint.sh: mkdir STORAGE_PATH, alembic upgrade head, exec uvicorn app.main:app on ${PORT:-8000}. It resolves the repository root from its own path, so the same file boots from the image, from a checkout and from a Procfile slug.
packaging.gate: RUN python3 scripts/release_gate.py inside the build: layout, console routes, packaging contract, bundle, models, boot on a throwaway store, committed openapi vs served routes, and the code-phase suite. A red suite cannot become a deployable image.
packaging.secrets: .dockerignore excludes .env/.env.local and local databases; every credential arrives from the platform environment, so no layer carries one
packaging.service_boot_artifacts: the gate's own /app/data is removed after the build: the image ships no database, and the runtime root is created and migrated on boot
packaging.user: root. The Render disk is mounted for the container user; a non-root user is a hardening follow-up that has to keep the mount writable (worth doing, not done here).
packaging.verified: docker is not installed on the build box (`which docker` exits 1), so the image was never built here and no successful `docker build` is claimed. What was run instead, in a fresh venv from requirements.txt + requirements-dev.txt: the console stage itself (npm ci exit 0, npx tsc --noEmit exit 0, npx vite build exit 0; the emitted dist/index.html references /console/assets/index-CP6ku3iL.js and /console/assets/index-mvQIC1Su.css), and the entrypoint exactly as ENTRYPOINT runs it, against empty throwaway STORAGE_PATHs on port 8931: all three alembic revisions applied to head (0003_conversation_corpus), GET /health 200 with process/persistent_disk/database/migrations all ok, GET /metrics 200, GET / 200, GET /console/ 404 (the bundle is a build artefact, present only after the image COPY), process stopped by the captured PID. The Dockerfile's own HEALTHCHECK command was then executed verbatim: exit 0 with PORT=8931 (the bound port) and exit 1 with PORT=9999, which is the check that the probe follows $PORT. scripts/release_gate.py exits 0 (layout, console, packaging, bundle, models, boot, openapi, suite) and scripts/bench.py printed STORE_BENCH_P95_MS=283.0 (budget 500). The first place the Dockerfile runs end to end is the CI `image` job.

rollback.drill: scripts/rollback.sh writes the target revision to STORAGE_PATH/deploy_revision and prints the APP_REVISION/APP_MARK the restart needs (app/revision.py reports those two from the environment, so the restart is the change); boot applies alembic upgrade head, so the schema is not downgraded. The rollback drill itself is the factory's deploy_observe exercise (start rev-n, persist a row, start rev-n-plus-1 with a detectable mark, roll back to rev-n, assert prior health and prior data): no tests/test_deploy.py exists in this tree, and this stage does not claim to have run that outer drill.
rollback.render_equivalent: Dashboard rollback to the previous deploy; same disk

spof: SPOF: Render rollback restarts a prior image against the same single-instance disk. There is no replica and no multi-AZ handoff. Losing the disk loses live SQLite (platform.db) and same-disk backups. Rollback does not create HA. A prior image that cannot read a newer schema is an S10 concern; this stage rolls back process identity, not a second copy of the data.
